name: Modular Furniture Hardware
tagline: Hinges, drawers and channels — the parts a client judges you on
description: Hardware is where a kitchen quietly succeeds or fails. Boards last; it is the hinge that sags and the channel that grinds after two years. This section follows the way the major brands structure their own catalogues: hinges, drawer systems and channels, each specified by load, opening angle and closing behaviour.

materials.name: Soft-close hinge
materials.blurb: Integrated damper — the shutter never slams
materials.description: A hydraulic damper built into the hinge cup slows the last few degrees of travel. Now the baseline expectation on any paid kitchen job; the cheap non-damped alternative is false economy.

materials.name: Concealed hinge
materials.blurb: Hidden inside the carcass — nothing visible when closed
materials.description: The standard European cup hinge, invisible with the door shut and adjustable in three planes after installation. Everything else in modular joinery is built around its 35 mm cup.

materials.name: Push-to-open hinge
materials.blurb: Handle-less operation — press the shutter and it opens
materials.description: A mechanical or magnetic latch releases the door on a light press, which is what makes a truly handle-less kitchen possible. Needs consistent gapping, so it demands better site accuracy than a handled scheme.

materials.name: 90° hinge
materials.blurb: Restricted opening for tight corners and appliance clearances
materials.description: Limits the shutter to a right angle so it cannot foul an adjacent wall, appliance or window reveal. A detail worth catching at drawing stage rather than on site.

materials.name: 110° hinge
materials.blurb: The everyday opening angle for standard shutters
materials.description: The volume seller: enough swing for comfortable access without the shutter projecting into a walkway. Specify it as the default and use wider angles only where drawers must clear.

materials.name: 155° hinge
materials.blurb: Wide opening so internal drawers clear the shutter
materials.description: Needed wherever a pull-out basket or internal drawer sits behind a hinged door — at 110° the shutter blocks the run. Also used on corner and pantry units.

materials.name: 165° hinge
materials.blurb: Near-flat opening for bi-fold and blind-corner units
materials.description: Opens almost against the carcass, which is what a blind-corner or bi-fold arrangement needs to give full access. Heavier and dearer, so use it only where the geometry demands it.

materials.name: Tandem drawer
materials.blurb: Concealed under-mount runners with full extension and soft close
materials.description: The runner sits under the drawer box and disappears from view, giving a clean interior and full access to the back. The current benchmark for a mid-to-premium kitchen.

materials.name: Slim drawer system
materials.blurb: Thin metal sides that maximise usable width
materials.description: A slim steel side profile replaces a thick timber box, so more of the cabinet opening becomes storage. Looks precise and modern with a matching internal organiser.

materials.name: Double-wall drawer
materials.blurb: Steel-sided box that assembles fast and stays square
materials.description: The drawer box arrives as a metal system rather than built on site — quicker to install, dimensionally exact and easy to add railings or glass sides to.

materials.name: Heavy-duty drawer
materials.blurb: Rated for 60–100 kg — grain storage and appliance drawers
materials.description: Reinforced runners for the drawers that get loaded hard: grain and pulse storage, tool drawers and pull-out appliance platforms. Check the rating against a full drawer, not an empty one.

materials.name: Under-mount channel
materials.blurb: Runner hidden beneath the drawer base
materials.description: Nothing visible from inside the drawer, so the box reads as one clean volume. Requires accurate carcass work — the tolerance for error is far smaller than with a side-mounted channel.

materials.name: Telescopic channel
materials.blurb: Ball-bearing side channel — the everyday workhorse
materials.description: The most common drawer runner in India: side-mounted, full extension, easy to fit and easy to replace. Good value where the drawer interior will not be on show.

materials.name: Soft-close channel
materials.blurb: Telescopic channel with a damper on the closing stroke
materials.description: Adds the damped final travel to a standard side channel — the cheapest way to give a budget kitchen the feel clients associate with premium hardware.

materials.name: Push-open channel
materials.blurb: Handle-less drawers that release on a press
materials.description: The drawer equivalent of a push-to-open hinge, needed to keep a handle-less run consistent. Combine with soft close so it does not fly back at the user.

materials.name: Concealed channel
materials.blurb: Runner tucked into the drawer side, out of sight
materials.description: A middle path between the visible telescopic channel and a full under-mount system: cleaner than the former, cheaper than the latter, and forgiving of ordinary site accuracy.
